cards.text: Jeremiah the prophet gets a word from the LORD about the nations, and it starts with Egypt. It's about the army of Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt. That army was defeated at Carchemish on the Euphrates River in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.

cards.question: Pharaoh Neco's army was defeated at Carchemish. Who defeated it?

cards.text: Then the message drops us onto a battlefield with orders flying: shields up, harness the horses, helmets on, polish the spears, armor on, advance for battle! That is a whole CHECKLIST, friend, and somebody back there is holding a clipboard.

cards.question: Egypt's army is geared up and ready. Then the LORD says, "Why am I seeing this?" What is He seeing?

cards.text: Terrified. Retreating. Fleeing in a hurry without looking back, with terror on every side. One verse they're polishing spears, and the next they're moving like somebody leaving work at 5:00 on a Friday.

cards.question: In this battle, Egypt's fastest soldiers manage to get away.
Egypt's warriors stumble and fall in the north, by the River Euphrates.

cards.text: Then the message asks a question: "Who is this, rising like the Nile, like rivers whose waters churn?" Picture a river rising right up over its banks.

cards.question: Who's rising like a river? ___ rises like the Nile, and its waters churn like rivers.
Egypt rising like the Nile comes with a boast. What does Egypt boast it will do?

answers.text: Cover the earth and destroy cities
Build a wall around its borders

cards.text: Then the orders start up again: "Advance, O horses! Race furiously, O chariots!" And the warriors get called out onto the field too.

cards.question: Warriors march out with Egypt, carrying shields and drawing bows. Where are they from?

cards.text: Here's the turn, friend. Egypt's been bragging and charging, but that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Hosts, and the sword will devour until it is satisfied.

cards.question: The day at Carchemish belongs to the Lord GOD of Hosts. It is a day of ___ against His foes.
The Lord GOD of Hosts will hold a sacrifice back home in Egypt, by the River Nile.

cards.text: Then the message speaks straight to Egypt and calls her the Virgin Daughter of Egypt. Go up to Gilead for balm, it tells her.

cards.question: Egypt is told to go up to Gilead for balm. She tries many remedies, but for her there is no ___.
After the battle at Carchemish, the other nations never hear about what happened to Egypt.
Egypt's outcry fills the earth, because warrior ___ over warrior and both of them have ___ together.

findings.problem: Card 1 already tells the baker that Egypt's army was defeated at Carchemish on the Euphrates River. That gives away card 7's statement that Egypt's warriors stumble and fall by the River Euphrates. Only 'in the north' is new, so the card tests nothing the baker hasn't just been told.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Verse 10's 'in the land of the north by the River Euphrates' repeats verse 6's 'In the north by the River Euphrates.' Card 7 already asked about it, and card 1 already told it. Card 15 asks about the same place a second time, so the answer is given away.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: Only cards 3 and 5 carry any of Papa Dorin's humor or personality. Cards 1, 8, 11, 13 and 16 read as plain narration of the text. Card 13 gets a 'Here's the turn, friend,' but the others have nothing a baker would repeat to a friend. Cards 11 (the horses and chariots charging out) and 16 (Egypt sent to Gilead for balm that won't work) could carry a reverent laugh without muddying a fact.

rule.text: Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
